Forecast Discussion

The evening weather map is relaxing our heat pump ridge in the Atlantic. This allows height falls to approach Western North Carolina from the northwest in between the stronger ridge over the southwestern states. This pattern shift will lead to a break in the heat and difficult to time multiple episodes of showers and thunderstorms.

Waves of moisture from the west roll showers and thunderstorms through the region overnight. Friday is a humid, cooler, and wetter day as an approaching front helps to kick up extra activity. After morning showers move out, most of the showers & storms will focus on the afternoon.

The front moves by overnight, but it is not stout enough to clean out all the junk for Saturday (just most of it). A couple of morning showers are possible, then widely scattered PM showers return ahead of a reinforcing shot of cooler air.

Sunday’s front will make more of a difference. A few more lingering showers along the western escarpment scatter out as the day turns from partly cloudy to more sunny, and a less humid afternoon unfolds where high temperatures largely stay below 80 degrees. Morning lows will be much more cool & pleasant than they have been as of late. Dry weather persists through Wednesday morning, with showers returning that afternoon.
